title: DVGA GraphQL command-injection runner: approval-gated OS command evidence on local lab only
goal: Add a dedicated, approval-gated GraphQL command-injection validation capability that can safely prove the DVGA systemDiagnostics command-injection challenge on a local intentionally vulnerable lab, without folding OS command execution into the generic graphql-probe runner.
scope: Follow-up from backlog-242 DVGA live-lab validation. During the authorized DVGA proof, graphql-probe deliberately avoided the DVGA systemDiagnostics(cmd:) surface because the active task prohibited OS command execution and unrelated DVGA exploitation families. The operator explicitly requested a future task for that coverage because real pentest suites need controlled command-injection proof. This package captures that work as a separate governed slice with its own authorization, kill-switch, safe command allowlist, provenance, reporting, and local-lab acceptance.
generation_reason: The operator asked to create a separate task for DVGA GraphQL OS-command-injection coverage after backlog-242 kept systemDiagnostics out of the generic graphql-probe runner.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Implement only governed GraphQL command-injection detection and DVGA local-lab proof. Do not add arbitrary shell, persistence, credential attacks, public target execution, reverse shells, file write, lateral movement, privilege escalation, or broad RCE exploitation families.
constraints.authorized_root_only: Active validation must run only against a locally launched DVGA instance at http://127.0.0.1:5013/ or http://localhost:5013/ unless a future active task explicitly authorizes another target.
constraints.approval_and_roe: Use existing approval, scope, ROE, runtime binding, credential, and kill-switch gates. This runner must require intrusive/exploitation approval before any command-bearing payload is sent.
constraints.safe_command_allowlist: Use a minimal local-lab command allowlist such as id, whoami, uname -a, or echo aegispt-command-injection-proof. No destructive commands, shell metacharacter chains beyond the documented DVGA proof form, network callbacks, file writes, persistence, package installs, credential access, or environment dumps.

success_criteria: A dedicated command-injection runner or clearly named graphql command-injection mode exists separately from generic graphql-probe.
The runner is wired through existing orchestration, finding extraction, provenance, report/replay recipe, approval validation, and run profile flows without bypassing gates.
The runner refuses out-of-scope targets and requires explicit intrusive/exploitation authorization for command-bearing payloads.
The safe command allowlist is enforced and covered by tests.
A local DVGA Docker lab is launched and the runner proves the documented systemDiagnostics command-injection challenge using only an allowed harmless command.
Evidence records exact local target URL, command allowlist entry, request summary, structured artifact, normalized finding, and cleanup status.
No existing GraphQL runner/API tests regress.
must_not_touch: Public DVGA or PortSwigger targets without explicit active-task authorization
Reverse shell, persistence, credential attack, file write, lateral movement, or privilege escalation payloads

acceptance_criteria: Only the local DVGA lab root is used for live command-injection acceptance.
The command-bearing payload uses an allowlisted harmless command and produces structured proof without destructive effects.
The run path remains approval-gated, scope-enforced, provenance-backed, and kill-switch compatible.
Any unsupported command-injection scenario is recorded as product truth with bounded follow-up rather than hidden behind green fixtures.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the only active task.
after_completion: Promote exactly one next approved task into NEXT_TASK.md.

out_of_scope: Running command payloads against public or customer targets without explicit active-task authorization
Reverse shells, callback/OOB command proof, persistence, arbitrary file write, package install, credential extraction, privilege escalation, or lateral movement
Merging command execution into generic graphql-probe discovery checks
Bypassing approval, scope, ROE, credentials, runtime binding, or kill-switch controls
